newsitem.title: DUBAI: Qatar says Israel at summit if peace talks revive.
newsitem.headline: Qatar says Israel at summit if peace talks revive.

text.p: Qatar's foreign minister said Israel could be invited to a Middle East-North Africa (MENA) economic summit in Doha in November if it changed its position in Arab-Israeli peace talks.
Asked if Israel would be invited, Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jabr al-Thani said it was too early to talk about Israel's attendance, the official Saudi Press Agency (SPA) said on Sunday.

"Based on progress in the peace process...and in case there is an improvement in the peace process and a change in the Israeli position then it would be possible to extend an invitation to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to attend the conference," it quoted him saying.
Sheikh Hamad was speaking at a news conference at the end of a two-day meeting of Gulf Arab foreign ministers in the Saudi capital Riyadh late on Saturday, SPA said.
Doha -- which has trade links with Israel -- is hosting the conference, the fourth since landmark peace negotiations began in 1991. Israel attended all three previous summits.
Syria and some Gulf Arab states favour postponing the MENA summit, attended by Israel, Arab and Western countries, until Middle East peace talks resume, diplomats and official Gulf sources have said.
But Sheikh Hamad said Arab states would benefit from the summit: "The summit will not force anyone to deal with Israel or support dealing with Israel."
